summary: PUCO-approved tariff (July 9, 2025, effective July 23): 25 MW+ data centers pay at least 85% of subscribed capacity for up to 12 years (4-year ramp), with an exit fee equal to three years of minimum charges; under appeal at the Ohio Supreme Court

IURC-approved settlement (order February 19, 2025): 80% minimum billing demand and 12-year minimum contracts after a 5-year ramp; signed by Amazon, Microsoft, Google, the Data Center Coalition, and consumer advocates
Georgia PSC rule effective February 1, 2025: new 100 MW+ customers take custom contracts with minimum billing, terms up to 15 years, and PSC review 30 days before execution

SCC-approved GS-5 class (November 25, 2025, effective January 1, 2027): 25 MW+ customers pay at least 85% of contracted distribution and transmission demand plus 60% of generation demand, minimum 14-year contracts, $1.5M/MW collateral

OPUC-approved Schedule 96 (May 7, 2026) under the POWER Act: 90% minimum demand charge, 100% of distribution upgrades paid by the customer, 10-30 year contracts, and a 1 cent/kWh surcharge above 100 MW funding low-income energy programs

Large Load Power Service plan approved 4-0 (effective Dec 13, 2025) implementing SB 4: 75 MW+ eligibility, minimum monthly bill with an 80% demand-charge floor, 12-year minimum terms plus up to a 5-year ramp, exit charges and a cost stabilization rider
source_name: Missouri PSC Report and Order, Case EO-2025-0154

summary: Rate GPD data-center provisions: 100 MW threshold (or 100 MW aggregated across 20 MW+ common-owner sites), 15-year minimum contracts, 80% minimum billing demand, ramp of up to 5 years, automatic 5-year extensions absent 4 years' notice
source_name: Michigan PSC news release, Case U-21859

summary: Economic-development rate riders (Schedules 33A/33B) approved by settlement for a 100 MW+ data center, with a floor at the utility's incremental cost. A negotiated economic-development rate rather than a restrictive large-load tariff, noted for honesty. A follow-on update (Docket 59948) was pending as of mid-2026

docket: SCC order on Dominion Rider T1 transmission cost allocation (July 31, 2026)
summary: Mandatory contribution in aid of construction directly assigning the cost of substations and transmission lines built to serve new direct-connect large loads (data centers foremost) to those customers instead of all ratepayers. Cut the residential share of Dominion's ~$1.5B Rider T1 filing from $2.90 to $0.94 a month, and the SCC flagged a future docket on assigning more upstream transmission costs
